source: FIGURES.md adapted from people to clubs, 11 September 2026. S1 search demand: Ahrefs GB, a name counts when it is searched in its own right at GB >= 100 or global >= 500, collisions excluded. S2 also_talk_about on 'best clubs in london' and 'clubs in london'. S3 People Also Ask and the questions pull (Blitz is the only club named). S4 the consensus lists actually read: RA guide (13 clubs), Time Out 'best clubs in London' updated 29 July 2026 (40), Conde Nast Traveller (12, via curl), ICMP 'A History of London Nightclubs' (30, ranks 6 for famous clubs in london). Not read: visitlondon (403), tripadvisor (403), luxlifelondon (bot wall). S5 English Wikipedia: Acid house, Second Summer of Love, Heaven (nightclub), Jungle music, Dubstep, UK garage, Blitz Kids (New Romantics). S6 the catalogue: not applicable, it has no venue field, and by the owner's rule of 11 September 2026 it is not a criterion. The End and the Blue Note are required by owner decision (2026-09-11), the owner's standing counting as a source as it did for Sisyphos. Facts re-checked 2026-09-11 against Wikipedia: Nicky Holloway, London Astoria, Shoom, Metalheadz, The End (club), Fabric (club), Ministry of Sound, Corsica Studios, The Cause (London), Printworks (London), Fold (nightclub), Drumsheds, The Four Aces Club, Scala (club), Trash (nightclub). Rule: required means 3+ sources or S5 at all; optional 2; rejected 1 and not S5. The Wikipedia category 'Nightclubs in London' and Google's local pack were read as coverage checks and are not counted as sources.

required_records.title: Heaven
required_records.why: opened December 1979 by Jeremy Norman; Spectrum (Oakenfold, Ian St Paul, Apr 1988-1990), Rage (Kevin Millins, Oct 1988-1993, Fabio & Grooverider), The Land of Oz, Megatripolis; also a garage room (S5). The single room that carries acid house, jungle and garage. Rage's place in jungle has a second source: the Metalheadz article says Kemistry took Goldie to Rage and it shaped him
